heading: Integrated title bar
body:
With `"titleBar": "integrated"` in `tac.application.window`, a macOS app shows one continuous surface: the page reaches the top edge of the window, and the real close, minimize and full screen buttons sit on the page. The window keeps its title for VoiceOver, Mission Control and the Window menu; only the text is hidden. The optional `titleBarButtonInset` moves the buttons, in points from the leading and top edges (0 to 200 each). The default is `"standard"`. Any other `titleBar` value, a `titleBarButtonInset` without `"titleBar": "integrated"`, a value above 200 or an unknown key in the inset stops the build with `TY1601`.

The host tells the page how much room the buttons need with three CSS custom properties: `--tac-titlebar-height`, `--tac-titlebar-leading-inset` and `--tac-titlebar-trailing-inset`. It updates them when the window is resized, enters or leaves full screen, or changes appearance. In full screen they are `0px`, because macOS shows the title bar over the page only when the pointer reaches the top of the screen. A browser sets none of them, so always write a fallback, such as `max(16px, var(--tac-titlebar-leading-inset, 0px))`. Draw the page in both light and dark colors (for example with `light-dark()`); the title bar area shows the page background, so there is no strip of another color.

The page now covers the area that moves the window, so mark that area with `data-tac-drag-region`. Dragging it moves the window, and a double-click does what System Settings says for a title bar double-click (fill, zoom, minimize or nothing). Links, buttons, form fields, focusable elements and anything marked `data-tac-no-drag` inside the region keep their clicks. The rest of the page is never a drag area. On Linux the same manifest gives the same contract: the page reaches the top edge, GTK's own window buttons sit on it in the desktop's button layout (so the close button may be on either side, and the trailing inset is often the larger one), the three properties and drag regions work as above, and a double-click follows the desktop's title bar setting. The menu bar moves into a main menu button beside the window buttons, as in GNOME apps, and `titleBarButtonInset` measures `leading` from the window edge where each group of buttons sits; the build prints a note saying so. On Windows the page reaches the top edge under the system minimize, maximize and close buttons, and the three properties hold their height and width (the leading inset is `0px`). WebView2 moves the window from drag regions, so a double-click maximizes or restores it and a right-click opens the window menu. The menu bar moves into the window menu (Alt+Space), and the window resizes from its sides and bottom, because the page covers the top edge. Windows cannot move its caption buttons, so it ignores `titleBarButtonInset` and the build prints a note. iOS and Android keep the standard status bar; the build prints a note. See ADR 0098.
